“She is not white, she is Latina”: positionality as an asset in cross-cultural ethnographic research with First Nations youth in Australia
journal: International Journal of the Sociology of Language
abstract: Abstract This paper examines how my researcher positionality as a female migrant from the Global South became an asset when carrying out a sociolinguistic ethnography with First Nations girls at an Australian boarding school. In other sociolinguistic school ethnographies, most researchers have either worked within their own sociocultural communities, and/or tried to minimise their presence by not disclosing much about themselves. Here, following a culturally safe approach, I interrogate whether traditional approaches are culturally appropriate. I reflect on how I found ways to align with participants beyond shared cultural practices, and encourage other (socio)linguists to engage with reflexivity and positionality in their work to make visible from which standpoint(s) knowledge is being produced.

title: Visibility management and profile construction on Tinder
abstract: Purpose This article examines how visibility and recognizability are configured through self-presentation on Tinder. It conceptualizes visibility management as a framework for examining the degree and form of exposure through which users become available for recognition and evaluation within a platform environment. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on digital ethnography and qualitative analysis of 100 Tinder profiles, the study examines recurrent configurations of facial and bodily recognizability, visual concealment and other forms of visual and textual disclosure. The corpus consists of female profiles presented to two research accounts in the Barcelona area in 2023. Findings The findings identify three modes of profile presentation: concealment, negotiation and integration. These modes capture different configurations of exposure and recognizability. Concealment substantially restricts physical recognizability while retaining varying forms of visual or textual disclosure; negotiation combines recognizable and obscured elements within the same profile; and integration combines comparatively high physical recognizability with curated lifestyle representation. Rather than operating through a simple opposition between visibility and concealment, these modes indicate a continuum in which bodily exposure, facial recognizability and other forms of disclosure vary independently and in combination. Research limitations/implications The findings are based on qualitative analysis of 100 profiles visible within a specific demographic and geographic configuration of Tinder. The corpus consists exclusively of female profiles presented within a 10 km radius in the Barcelona area in 2023 and should not be interpreted as representative of Tinder users more broadly or as evidence of gender-independent patterns. Future research could combine profile analysis with interviews, comparative platform studies or cross-cultural approaches to further examine visibility management across digital environments and across different gender and sexual-orientation configurations. Originality/value The article reframes Tinder self-presentation as a form of visibility management. It distinguishes visibility management from self-presentation and impression management by foregrounding how different degrees and forms of exposure make users available for recognition and evaluation. The three empirically derived modes contribute to this framework by conceptualizing visibility as a continuum of recognizability and disclosure rather than a binary condition.

Técnica y edición de vídeo y sonido. Introducción al vídeo y a la inteligencia artificial aplicada a la comunicación audiovisual [Libro completo]
journal: Espejo de Monografías de Comunicación Social
abstract: La industria audiovisual atraviesa uno de los procesos de transformación más profundos de su historia. La convergencia entre producción digital, plataformas de streaming, redes sociales, inteligencia artificial y nuevas formas de consumo mediático ha redefinido las competencias que deben adquirir los futuros profesionales de la comunicación. La formación universitaria enfrenta el desafío de integrar conocimientos teóricos, competencias técnicas, pensamiento crítico y capacidades de adaptación tecnológica.Ya no resulta suficiente dominar cámaras, programas de edición o técnicas narrativas tradicionales; es imprescindible comprender cómo los procesos audiovisuales se articulan en ecosistemas digitales complejos donde convergen creatividad, tecnología, datos e inteligencia artificial.Técnica y edición de vídeo y sonido. Introducción al vídeo y a la inteligencia artificial aplicada a la comunicación audiovisual responde a estas necesidades formativas. Se trata de un manual concebido para acompañar al estudiante durante todo el proceso de aprendizaje, desde los fundamentos del lenguaje audiovisual hasta la construcción de un portafolio profesional orientado a la empleabilidad.El texto combina rigor académico, orientación práctica y actualización tecnológica, ofreciendo una propuesta integral alineada con los principios del Espacio Europeo de Educación Superior y con las demandas actuales de la industria audiovisual internacional.

title: Redefining senior workforce management: challenges, opportunities and strategic pathways
journal: European Journal of Training and Development
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify and analyse the emerging challenges that will shape the development of senior talent in the coming years and, crucially, to provide a multi-level and context-sensitive framework for interpreting these challenges responsibly. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a qualitative–computational design combining collective artificial intelligence (CAI) with a two-stage analytical process involving 306 Spanish management staff. A theoretical framework integrates structural, organisational and individual perspectives (theory of ageism, human capital theory, theory of social capital, theory of cognitive ageing and a variety of psychosocial approaches). CAI algorithms (conceptual stratification, semantic clustering, hybridisation and pairwise comparison) enable the aggregation, synthesis and prioritisation of expert judgements. Findings The findings reveal two main areas of challenge: (1) ensuring that senior employees adapt and remain essential in organisational transformation – addressing issues of strategy, motivation, roles, digitalisation and humility – and (2) enabling them to feel valued and to pass on their legacy, which involves addressing knowledge transfer, recognition, ageism, rewards and work–life balance. This study highlights the most widely supported initiatives and the differences found based on gender, age and professional profile. It also offers a set of winning strategies and key proposals for effective management of senior talent. Originality/value This study identifies emerging, system-level patterns that cut across structural, organisational and individual domains, offering a forward-looking understanding of the challenges shaping senior talent development. The use of CAI enhances analytical depth by integrating diverse perspectives, generating consensus-based insights and revealing complex challenges that traditional qualitative or Delphi-based methods may overlook. By combining this methodological innovation with a multi-level theoretical framework, this study provides organisations with a theoretically grounded and context-sensitive roadmap for transforming senior-related challenges into strategic opportunities.

title: Knowledge management and project performance: a quasi-experimental study in EPC oil and gas projects
abstract: Purpose This study addresses two interconnected gaps in project-based knowledge management (KM) research: the absence of prescriptive, stage-specific intervention frameworks for Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) projects, and the lack of causal evidence linking digital KM interventions to objective operational outcomes. Design/methodology/approach An integrated practical framework for knowledge transfer in EPC projects is developed by embedding Szulanski's knowledge transfer model within the EPC disciplinary structure; its Stage 2–4 mechanisms are validated through a quasi-experimental Difference-in-Differences design using longitudinal administrative data from 12 welders over eight weeks in an international oil and gas EPC project in Iraq. Findings The framework's prescribed mechanisms produce a 4.4% increase in production efficiency, a 21% reduction in defect rates and a 17% decrease in safety incidents simultaneously (p < 0.001). These findings are consistent with infrastructural barriers playing a substantial role in fragmented EPC environments, and all mechanisms are operationalisable through an easy-to-deploy, cloud-based platform requiring no specialist development. Originality/value First, the study develops an integrated practical framework that transforms Szulanski's descriptive typology into a prescriptive design tool specifying stage-specific and discipline-specific knowledge management system mechanisms. Second, it provides causal validation of a KM framework using objective operational data, an evidentiary standard that perception-based studies cannot achieve. Third, it demonstrates that the framework's prescribed mechanisms are fully operationalisable through an easy-to-deploy, cloud-based platform requiring no specialist development, closing the gap between framework validity and framework adoptability that has historically limited the practical impact of KM research.
